title: Bias-weighted bidirectional LSTM toxicity classifier
summary: The solution tokenizes lowercased comments with a regex, truncates them to 220 tokens, and builds a training-derived vocabulary of up to 200,000 tokens occurring at least five times; padding and unknown IDs are reserved. A learned 256-dimensional embedding with spatial dropout feeds two stacked bidirectional LSTMs. Masked max and mean temporal pooling are concatenated, passed through two ReLU dense layers with a residual connection, and projected to one toxicity logit plus identity auxiliary logits. Training uses weighted binary cross-entropy for toxicity and unweighted binary cross-entropy for identity labels. Identity-mentioning examples and specified toxic/non-toxic subgroup combinations receive increased toxicity-loss weights, normalized by mean weight. Length-bucketed shuffled batches reduce padding. Adam optimization uses mixed-precision gradient scaling, gradient-norm clipping, and exponential learning-rate decay over four epochs. Inference batches validation texts by length and returns sigmoid-transformed toxicity logits.
